title: Bills in Order
subtitle: A Household Guide to Paying on Time and Catching Up When You Fall Behind
description_paragraphs: Most bills aren't paid late because someone didn't care. They're paid late because due dates are scattered across the month, notices arrive by mail, email and app, an autopay runs from an account nobody checks, and paydays don't line up with any of it. Bills in Order is a plain-language guide to bringing all of that together, and to knowing the next step when a payment slips or the money doesn't stretch.

You'll build a system for your own home, on paper, in a spreadsheet or in your bank's own tools, that shows you for every bill whether it is paid, due or missing, without relying on memory. One short chapter at a time, each ending with a single step for the week, the book takes you from finding every recurring bill, the yearly ones included, to lining due dates up with your paydays and deciding what runs on autopay and what you check by hand.

It's written for the adult who handles the bills in an American home: a parent juggling utilities, rent or a mortgage, a couple of cards and a few subscriptions; a retiree who pays some bills by autopay and some by check; someone just hit by a late fee who wants a routine that holds; and the grown child or partner taking over the bills for someone who can no longer manage them. You don't need to enjoy money matters or know the vocabulary: every term is explained the first time it appears.

When things go wrong, it stays calm and practical: what happens in the first days after a missed payment and what you can do about it, how to ask for a fee to be waived or for more time before a due date, what each kind of bill puts at stake when money runs short, where to find utility assistance, nonprofit credit counseling and legal aid, and how to catch up when several bills are behind. It explains how things generally work in the United States and says where the rules vary by state or provider. It is information, not financial or legal advice, and it never judges you for being behind.

author_bio: Claire Halvorsen is a pen name. Bills in Order is written for the adult who handles the bills at home: plainly, without jargon and without judgment, with every unavoidable term explained the first time it appears. The book describes how bills, fees and options generally work in the United States, and it points readers to the provider, a nonprofit credit counselor or an attorney when their situation calls for one.
back_cover:
Paid, due or missing: for every bill in your home, you should be able to tell at a glance.

Bills in Order shows you how to build a simple system that does the remembering for you: one list of every recurring bill, one place where it lives, a calendar tied to your paydays and a short routine that keeps it current.

And when a payment slips or the money isn't there, it gives you a calm next step: what each bill puts at stake, whom to call, what to ask for and where to find help, without lectures and without judgment.

General information for U.S. households, not financial or legal advice.
